mainTopic: משה's oath, the flat-backed snake, the clashing oaths on one loaf, and a new משנה on who is bound by שבועת ביטוי and שבועת שוא, including שמואל's rule that answering אמן counts as swearing.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: משה tied the people's oath to his own mind and God's so that it could never be undone through הפרה. The גמרא then explains the משנה's 'snake like an olive-press beam' example of a שבועת שוא. שמואל says it means a snake whose back is flat, and no such snake exists. Next, for someone who swore to eat a loaf and then swore not to eat it, רבי ירמיה reads the משנה as saying that not eating makes him liable also for the שבועת ביטוי. A new משנה teaches that both שבועת ביטוי and שבועת שוא bind everyone, in or out of בית דין. Breaking either on purpose brings מלקות, but only a mistaken שבועת ביטוי brings a קרבן עולה ויורד. Both oaths count even when someone else says the oath and the person answers אמן. שמואל learns this from the סוטה, who answers 'אמן אמן,' and the גמרא supports him from sources that seem to clash until we split them by whether אמן was answered. The פרק שבועות שתים then closes with הדרן.

steps.title: Why משה tied the oath to his own mind and God's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives its final reason for משה's wording: it was so that the people's oath could never be undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, משה made them swear 'on my mind and God's mind' so that there could be no undoing of their oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion. It explains that משה worded the oath this way so that no one could later have it undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier idea was that משה feared the people would swear with a private meaning in their heads. The גמרא sets that idea aside with 'אלא' and gives a different reason. Tying the oath to the knowledge of משה and God made it an oath that cannot receive הפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this drops the earlier idea and brings a new one
So that ... not
Undoing or cancelling an oath or vow

steps.whatToRemember: משה's wording 'on my mind and God's mind' was meant to make the oath permanent, so it could never receive הפרה.

phrases.english: Rather, in order
that there should be no undoing of their oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא תִּהְוֵי הֲפָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the earlier part of the daf about משה's oath.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier reason with a new one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה worried the people would swear with a private meaning in mind.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה's wording was meant to block any future הפרה of the oath.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's example of the huge snake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's example of an impossible oath: 'If I did not see a snake like the beam of an olive press.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If I did not see a snake as big as the beam of an olive press.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה. It is setting up a question about it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, this is one example of a שבועת שוא: swearing that you saw something impossible. The גמרא is about to ask whether this really is impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: Snake
The heavy beam of an olive press
An oath taken in vain, such as swearing to something impossible or obviously false

phrases.english: And: 'If I did not see a snake
phrases.notes: In oath language, 'if I did not see' means 'I swear that I saw.'

phrases.english: like the beam of an olive press.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לֹא רָאִיתִי נָחָשׁ כְּקוֹרַת בֵּית הַבַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Swearing that you saw a snake like an olive-press beam is given as an example of a שבועת שוא.

steps.title: But there was a giant snake in the days of שבור מלכא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: such huge snakes do exist, since one in the days of שבור מלכא swallowed thirteen stables of straw.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are there really no such snakes? But in the years of King שבור there was one snake that swallowed thirteen stables full of straw!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the משנה's example. It says a snake that big is not impossible, because there was a famous huge one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath only counts as שבועת שוא if what it claims is impossible. If giant snakes really exist, then swearing you saw one might be true. In that case the משנה's example would not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it not so?! A surprised challenge
But look! It brings a fact that contradicts what was said
King שבור, a Persian king
Straw

phrases.english: And there are none?!
But there was that one which existed
in the years of King שבור,
there was one that held
phrases.notes: 'Held' here means it swallowed that much into its belly.

phrases.english: thirteen stables of straw!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא?! וְהָא הַהוּא דַּהֲוָה בִּשְׁנֵי שַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the example quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that a snake like an olive-press beam is impossible
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A snake even bigger than that did exist, so the oath could be true and is not שבועת שוא.

steps.title: שמואל: the comparison is about flatness, not size
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the משנה is not talking about size. It means a snake that is flat like the beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: it means a flat snake.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge. The oath claims the snake was flat like the beam, which is the impossible part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the comparison to the beam was about size. שמואל changes what is being compared: shape, not size. Big snakes exist, but a snake shaped flat like a beam does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Flat

phrases.english: שמואל said: It refers to a flat one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the case: the comparison is about shape, not size
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Like the beam' means as big as the beam.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Like the beam' means flat like the beam.

steps.title: But all snakes are flat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to שמואל: every snake is flat, so a flat snake is nothing impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: But all snakes are flat too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל's answer. Flat snakes are normal, so swearing you saw one would not be impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If flatness is ordinary for snakes, שמואל's answer brings back the same problem. The oath would be true, not שבועת שוא.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them as well
They are certainly flat

phrases.english: All of them are also flat!
phrases.notes: The underside of a snake is flat, so every snake has a flat side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's explanation that the משנה means a flat snake
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Flatness is normal for snakes, so a flat snake is not impossible.

steps.title: A snake whose back is flat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the answer: the משנה means a snake whose back is flat, and that does not exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means a snake whose back is flat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens שמואל's answer. The impossible snake is one that is flat on top, on its back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A snake is flat underneath, but its back is rounded. A snake flat on its back like a wooden beam is impossible. So the oath really is a שבועת שוא.

keyTerms.meaning: Its back

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's snake 'like an olive-press beam' means a snake flat on its back, which does not exist. That is why the oath is שבועת שוא.

phrases.english: It refers to one whose back is flat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by narrowing שמואל's answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Flat' means flat in general, which every snake is.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Flat' means flat on its back, which no snake is.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about two clashing oaths on one loaf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a person who swore to eat a loaf and then swore not to eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'I swear I will eat this loaf,' then 'I swear I will not eat it,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. It is setting up a question about the ruling there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that the first oath is a שבועת ביטוי and the second is a שבועת שוא. If he eats, he is liable for the שבועת שוא. If he does not eat, he is liable for breaking the שבועת ביטוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A loaf of bread
An oath about doing or not doing something, such as eating
Etc.; the rest of the משנה is assumed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two oaths. The first, 'I will eat,' is a real שבועת ביטוי. The second, 'I will not eat,' clashes with the first, so it is the שבועת שוא.

phrases.english: 'An oath that I will eat this loaf,'
'An oath that I will not eat it,' etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה: the first is a שבועת ביטוי, the second a שבועת שוא.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁאוֹכַל כִּכָּר זוֹ שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא אוֹכְלֶנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he does not eat, he is liable for breaking the שבועת ביטוי. If he eats, he is liable for the שבועת שוא.

steps.title: Shouldn't he also be liable for the vain oath?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if he did not eat, why is he only liable for the שבועת ביטוי? The second oath was already a שבועת שוא the moment he said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, he is liable for breaking the שבועת ביטוי, but not for the שבועת שוא? But an oath in vain came out of his mouth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling for the case where he does not eat. It argues he should be liable for both oaths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swearing 'I will not eat' contradicted the oath he already had to keep, so it was a שבועת שוא as soon as he said it. That sin does not depend on whether he later eats. So when he does not eat, he should be liable twice: for breaking the first oath and for the vain second oath.

keyTerms.meaning: Now; it opens a 'how can it be' argument
He is liable
But it already came out of his mouth

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge raises a key question: is a שבועת שוא counted when the words are spoken, or only when the person acts on them?

phrases.english: Now, he is liable because of the oath on an utterance,
phrases.notes: This is the case where he did not eat the loaf.

phrases.english: but he is not liable because of the vain oath?!
But an oath in vain has already been uttered!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling quoted in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that if he does not eat, he is liable only for the שבועת ביטוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second oath was a שבועת שוא as soon as he said it, so he should also be liable for it even if he does not eat.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה fixes the reading: also liable for שבועת ביטוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers the question from step 8. He reads the משנה as saying that the one who did not eat is also liable for שבועת ביטוי, on top of the שבועת שוא he already made.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Read the משנה like this: he is also liable for שבועת ביטוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question by changing how we read the משנה. He adds the word "also" (אף).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that the second oath was a שבועת שוא from the moment he said it. So why does the משנה mention only שבועת ביטוי? רבי ירמיה agrees the שוא is already there. He says the משנה means that if he does not eat, he also breaks his first oath to eat, which is a שבועת ביטוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too. It adds one more liability on top of the one already there.

steps.whatToRemember: If he does not eat, he gets both: the שבועת שוא from swearing against his first oath, and also the שבועת ביטוי for breaking the first oath.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: Teach it this way:
also for the oath on an utterance.
phrases.notes: He means: on top of the שבועת שוא he already made, not eating also breaks his first oath to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי ירמיה תני אף על שבועת ביטוי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 by fixing the wording of the משנה from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: adding "also" (אף) to the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that the one who did not eat is liable only for שבועת ביטוי, which ignores the שבועת שוא he already made.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is liable for שבועת שוא from when he swore, and also for שבועת ביטוי when he does not eat.

steps.title: New משנה: who is bound by שבועת ביטוי and its punishments
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that שבועת ביטוי applies to every kind of person, in court or out of court. Doing it on purpose brings lashes, and doing it by mistake brings a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: שבועת ביטוי applies to men and women, to relatives and non-relatives, to people who are fit to be witnesses and people who are not, in front of a בית דין or not, when he swears on his own. If he breaks it on purpose he gets מלקות, and if he breaks it by mistake he brings a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists who can be bound by שבועת ביטוי and the punishment for breaking it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is very wide on purpose: anyone who swears on his own is bound, with no limits. The משנה also gives two outcomes. Breaking it knowingly brings lashes. Breaking it by mistake brings a sliding-scale קרבן, where the animal or flour offering depends on how much the person can afford.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, meaning "our משנה". It marks the start of a new משנה.
Applies to / is in force for.
People who are not allowed to be witnesses.
Doing it on purpose, knowingly.
Doing it by mistake, without knowing.
A sliding-scale offering. The rich bring an animal, the poor bring birds, and the very poor bring flour.

steps.confusionAlert: Why list relatives and people who cannot be witnesses? These limits matter for שבועת העדות, the oath about testimony taught in the next פרק. The משנה is stressing that they do not apply to שבועת ביטוי.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The oath on an utterance applies
to men and to women,
to relatives and to non-relatives,
to those fit to testify and to those disqualified,

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין –
phrases.english: in the presence of a court and not in the presence of a court,
from his own mouth.
And they are liable for doing it on purpose to lashes,
and for doing it by mistake to a sliding-scale offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתני׳ שבועת ביטוי נוהגת באנשים ובנשים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion has been settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבועת ביטוי binds everyone, in court or out. On purpose brings מלקות; by mistake brings a קרבן עולה ויורד.

steps.title: שבועת שוא: same people, but no קרבן for a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the same wide list for שבועת שוא. Breaking it on purpose brings lashes, but breaking it by mistake brings nothing (פטור).
steps.simpleTranslation: שבועת שוא applies to men and women, to non-relatives and relatives, to people who are fit to be witnesses and people who are not, in front of a בית דין or not, and when he swears on his own. If he does it on purpose he gets מלקות, and if he does it by mistake he is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the same list of people for שבועת שוא. It then shows one difference in the punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Who is bound is exactly the same as for שבועת ביטוי. The difference is only in the mistake case. A mistaken שבועת ביטוי brings a קרבן, but a mistaken שבועת שוא brings no קרבן at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A useless or false oath, like swearing about something everyone knows is true or impossible.
Lashes, the punishment of מלקות.
Exempt, owes nothing.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main difference the משנה draws between the two oaths: only שבועת ביטוי done by mistake brings a קרבן.

phrases.english: The oath in vain applies
to men and to women,
to non-relatives and to relatives,
to those fit to testify and to those disqualified,

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין –
phrases.english: in the presence of a court and not in the presence of a court,
and from his own mouth.
And they are liable for doing it on purpose to lashes,
and for doing it by mistake he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same pattern as step 10, now for שבועת שוא, and shows the difference in the mistake case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבועת שוא binds everyone. On purpose brings מלקות; by mistake he is פטור, with no קרבן.

steps.title: Answering אמן to someone else's oath counts as swearing
steps.stepSummary: For both kinds of oath, a person who is made to swear by someone else is liable just as if he swore himself. This applies when he answers אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: For both this one and that one, a person made to swear by others is liable. For example, he said "I did not eat today" or "I did not put on תפילין today," and someone said "I make you swear," and he answered "אמן." He is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that the oath does not have to come from the person's own mouth. Saying אמן to an oath someone else gives him is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 10 and 11 spoke about swearing "from his own mouth." Now the משנה widens this. If someone else words the oath and he answers אמן, the oath counts as his own, for both שבועת ביטוי and שבועת שוא.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone made to swear by other people, who say the oath words.
"I make you swear": the words used to put an oath on someone.
Answering אמן means agreeing to the oath, and it counts as swearing.
תפילין, used here as an example of something a person may claim he did or did not do.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that אמן is just a polite reply. Here it is the act of swearing itself, so the person is fully liable if the statement was false.
steps.whatToRemember: Both oaths bind everyone, whether sworn on your own or by saying אמן to someone else's words. The only difference is that a mistaken שבועת ביטוי brings a קרבן and a mistaken שבועת שוא does not.

phrases.english: Both this one and that one,
phrases.notes: Both kinds of oath: שבועת ביטוי and שבועת שוא.

phrases.english: one who is made to swear by others is liable.
"If I did not eat today,"
or "I did not put on tefillin today,"
and someone said "I make you swear,"
and he said "Amen": he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אחת זו ואחת זו המושבע מפי אחרים חייב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens "from his own mouth" in steps 10 and 11 to include an oath someone else words, answered with אמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For both שבועת ביטוי and שבועת שוא, answering אמן to an oath given by someone else makes him liable, just as if he swore himself.

steps.title: Answering אמן counts like swearing yourself
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that answering אמן after an oath is like saying the oath with your own mouth. His source is the סוטה, who says אמן אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל said: anyone who answers 'אמן' after an oath is like someone who says the oath with his own mouth. As it says: 'And the woman shall say: אמן, אמן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא on our משנה begins. שמואל explains why a person who is made to swear by someone else is liable: by answering אמן, it counts as his own oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12's משנה said that someone made to swear by others is liable like one who swore himself. שמואל gives the reason and the source. The סוטה never says the oath herself; the כהן says it and she answers אמן, and that is enough to bind her.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Amen': saying yes to and accepting what was just said
like one who says the oath with his own mouth
a woman suspected by her husband of being unfaithful, who is made to take an oath

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule behind every oath given by בית דין. The person answers אמן and is fully bound, even though he never said the oath words himself.

phrases.english: Gemara: Shmuel said:
Anyone who answers 'Amen' after an oath
is like one who says the oath with his own mouth,
as it is written: 'And the woman shall say: Amen, amen.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:22. This is the סוטה, who only answers אמן to the oath the כהן says to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר שמואל: כל העונה אמן אחר שבועה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason and the פסוק behind the משנה's rule in step 12 that one made to swear by others is liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Answering אמן after an oath counts as saying the oath yourself, learned from the סוטה.

steps.title: רב פפא brings support from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא, in the name of רבא, says a משנה and a ברייתא also support שמואל. He first quotes the משנה about שבועת העדות: when others make the witnesses swear, they are liable only if they deny in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said in the name of רבא: a careful reading of the משנה and a ברייתא also supports this. The משנה teaches: שבועת העדות applies to men and not women, to non-relatives and not relatives, to people fit to testify and not to those unfit. It applies only to people fit to testify. It applies both in בית דין and outside of בית דין when the witness swears on his own. But when others make them swear, they are not liable until they deny in בית דין. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא is setting up a proof for שמואל. He starts by quoting the first source, a משנה about witnesses who falsely swear they know nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important line is at the end. If the witness swears by himself, he is liable anywhere. But if others make him swear, he is liable only when it happens in בית דין. This detail is what will soon clash with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: a witness's false oath that he knows no testimony
a careful reading shows it; it can be proven from the exact wording
from his own mouth; he says the oath himself
from the mouth of others; someone else makes him swear
that they deny (knowing the testimony)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases at the end. 'In or out of בית דין' goes with swearing on your own. Being made to swear by others counts only in בית דין.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:
A careful reading of the mishna and a baraita also supports this,
phrases.notes: He means שמואל's rule about אמן.

phrases.english: as it teaches: The oath of testimony applies
to men and not to women,
to non-relatives and not to relatives,
to those fit and not to those unfit;
and it applies only to those fit to testify,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין –
phrases.english: and in front of a court and not in front of a court
when he swears on his own;
but when made to swear by others, they are not liable
until they deny it in court.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a proof from sources for שמואל's rule.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that answering אמן counts like swearing yourself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of רבי מאיר about שבועת העדות (the first of two sources).

steps.title: The ברייתא says they are liable even outside court
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא quotes a ברייתא of רבי מאיר. When witnesses are made to swear and answer אמן, they are liable whether in בית דין or not, and whether they swore on their own or were made to swear by others.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: how does שבועת העדות work? A man said to witnesses, 'Come and testify for me.' They said, 'We swear that we know no testimony for you.' Or they said, 'We know no testimony for you,' and he said, 'I make you swear,' and they said 'אמן.' Whether in בית דין or not, and whether on their own or made to swear by others, once they denied it, they are liable. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings the second source. It is also from רבי מאיר, and here they are liable even when others made them swear outside of בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that being made to swear by others counts only in בית דין. The ברייתא says it counts even outside. The difference to notice is that in the ברייתא the witnesses answered אמן.

keyTerms.meaning: come and testify for me
I make you swear
how? (in what case?)

phrases.english: And it is taught in a baraita:
The oath of testimony, how does it work?
He said to witnesses: 'Come and testify for me';
they said: 'We swear that we know no testimony for you,'

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: ״אֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִין לָךְ עֵדוּת״;
phrases.english: or they said: 'We know no testimony for you';
and he said: 'I make you swear,' and they said (to him): 'Amen'
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: whether in front of a court or not in front of a court,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ בֵּין מִפִּי אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: whether on their own or made to swear by others,
once they denied it, they are liable.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the second source, which seems to disagree with the משנה in step 14.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי מאיר, which includes answering אמן and makes them liable even outside בית דין.

steps.title: The two sources contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא points out that the משנה and the ברייתא, both from רבי מאיר, seem to say opposite things.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא points out the clash between the two sources he just quoted. This sets up his solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, being made to swear by others counts only in בית דין. In the ברייתא, it counts even outside בית דין. Both are רבי מאיר, so they cannot simply disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: they contradict each other

phrases.english: They contradict each other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the משנה (step 14) and the ברייתא (step 15) side by side and shows they clash.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the משנה and the ברייתא of רבי מאיר fit together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same תנא cannot say that an oath forced by others counts only in בית דין, and also that it counts outside בית דין.

steps.title: One case answered אמן, the other did not
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא solves the contradiction. The ברייתא, where they are liable even outside בית דין, is when the witnesses answered אמן. The משנה is when they did not answer אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this: this one is when he answered 'אמן,' and that one is when he did not answer 'אמן'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא solves the contradiction by splitting the cases. This solution is the proof for שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answering אמן makes it his own oath, so he is liable anywhere, just like one who swears on his own. Without אמן, only the seriousness of בית דין makes the oath count. So the only way to fit the sources together is שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, must we not learn from this?
who answered

steps.whatToRemember: With אמן, an oath forced by others counts anywhere. Without אמן, it counts only in בית דין.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this:
this one is when he answered 'Amen,'
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the ברייתא, where they are liable even outside בית דין.

phrases.english: and that one is when he did not answer 'Amen'?
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the משנה, which needs בית דין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא לאו שמע מינה: הא דענה אמן, הא דלא ענה אמן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 16, and in doing so proves שמואל's rule from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is talking about a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא look like they give opposite rules for an oath forced by others outside בית דין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is when they answered אמן, which counts like swearing yourself. The משנה is when they did not answer.

steps.title: The גמרא agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees with רב פפא's reading, so שמואל's rule is supported.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof. The sources do support שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answering אמן to an oath is like saying it yourself. This rule is now supported both by the פסוק of the סוטה and by the משנה and ברייתא of רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it; yes, that is correct

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: answering אמן after an oath counts like saying the oath yourself. This is proven from the סוטה and from the משנה and ברייתא together.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the solution and proof from step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Answering אמן to an oath someone else says to you makes you fully bound, as if you swore it yourself.

steps.title: Our משנה also hints at שמואל's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבינא, in the name of רבא, quotes the first part of our משנה on שבועת ביטוי. He reads 'from his own mouth' to mean that an oath said by others does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said in the name of רבא: our משנה here can also be read carefully to show this. It teaches: 'A שבועת ביטוי applies to men and women, relatives and non-relatives, those fit to testify and those not, in front of a בית דין and not in front of a בית דין, from his own mouth.' From his own mouth, yes. From the mouth of others, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a third support for שמואל, this time from the משנה of our own פרק. He points to the words 'from his own mouth' and reads them as excluding an oath said by others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous proof came from the משנה and ברייתא about witnesses. Now the source is the משנה about שבועת ביטוי. רבינא is only setting up half of the picture here: the first part of the משנה seems to say an oath said by others makes you exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: It is precise. Careful reading of the wording shows the point.
An oath where a person swears he will or will not do something, or that he did or did not do something.
From his own mouth. He said the oath himself.
From the mouth of others. Someone else said the oath to him.
People disqualified from serving as witnesses.

phrases.english: Ravina said in the name of Rava:
Our mishna here is also precise [and shows this] —
phrases.notes: 'Our mishna here' means the משנה of this פרק about שבועת ביטוי, not the witnesses' משנה from before.

phrases.english: for it teaches:
"An oath on an utterance applies
to men and to women,
to non-relatives and to relatives,
to those fit [to testify] and to those disqualified,

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין –
phrases.english: in front of a court and not in front of a court —
from his own mouth": yes,
from the mouth of others: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further support for שמואל after the proof from the witnesses' sources in steps 14-18.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that answering אמן to an oath said by others counts like saying it yourself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of our פרק on שבועת ביטוי, read through the words 'from his own mouth.'

steps.title: The end of the משנה seems to say the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The last part of the same משנה says that someone made to swear by others is liable. That clashes with the first part.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the last part of the משנה teaches: 'In both this case and that case, if he was made to swear by others, he is liable.' These two lines contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the same משנה, which makes a person liable even when others made him swear. It points out that this clashes with the first part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part said 'from his own mouth, yes; from others, no.' The last part says 'from others, liable.' The same משנה cannot hold both as they stand, so a way to tell the two cases apart is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא.
This and that. Here it means both kinds of oath discussed in the משנה.
Someone who is made to swear.
They contradict each other.

phrases.english: And it teaches in the last part:
"This and that,
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means שבועת ביטוי and שבועת שוא, the two oaths the משנה talks about.

phrases.english: if he is made to swear by others, he is liable."
They contradict each other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the last part of the משנה against the first part quoted in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two parts of the משנה about שבועת ביטוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first part exempts an oath said by others, but the last part makes it liable. On the surface, the two parts cannot both be right.

steps.title: The difference is whether he answered אמן
steps.stepSummary: The last part of the משנה is a case where he answered אמן. The first part is where he did not. This is exactly שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: So must we not learn from this that the last part is where he answered 'amen,' and the first part is where he did not answer 'amen'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the clash by splitting the cases. If the person answered אמן, he is liable even though others said the oath. If he stayed silent, he is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of fix רב פפא gave for the witnesses' sources. Because the only way to make the משנה work is to say that answering אמן counts, the משנה itself turns out to support שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, must we not learn from it. This introduces the conclusion the source forces on us.
He answered.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה says both 'from others, not liable' and 'from others, liable.' Answering אמן is what makes the difference, and that is just what שמואל said.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from it:
this [last part] is where he answered "amen,"
that [first part] is where he did not answer "amen"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 20, and the answer proves שמואל's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each part of the משנה is about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two parts of the משנה seemed to argue about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The last part is when he answered אמן, so he is liable. The first part is when he did not, so he is exempt.

steps.title: So what did שמואל add?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה already teaches this, the גמרא asks what שמואל's statement was for.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what is שמואל teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: Since a משנה already shows שמואל's rule, the גמרא asks why שמואל needed to say it at all. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא is not expected to repeat a rule that is already in a משנה. So once the proofs succeed, it looks as though שמואל's statement adds nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? The question asks what new point a statement adds.

phrases.english: But then Shmuel —
what is he teaching us?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא שְׁמוּאֵל מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the success of the proofs: if the משנה teaches it, why did שמואל say it?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point שמואל's statement adds, if the rule can already be learned from a משנה.

steps.title: שמואל was explaining the משנה's careful reading
steps.stepSummary: שמואל was spelling out what the משנה only hints at through careful reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is teaching us the careful reading of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה never says the rule openly. שמואל stated it clearly so we would know how to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule only comes out after noticing a contradiction and solving it. שמואל's job was to make that hidden point plain, so his statement is not wasted.

keyTerms.meaning: A careful reading. It is a point learned from the exact wording.

steps.whatToRemember: An אמורא's statement can be valuable even when a משנה already contains the rule, if the משנה only hints at it.

phrases.english: He is teaching us the careful reading of the mishna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל made clear a rule that the משנה only teaches through careful reading.

steps.title: הדרן: Closing שבועות שתים
steps.stepSummary: The פרק שבועות שתים comes to an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, שבועות שתים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the פרק. It marks the end of שבועות שתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן shows a wish to come back and learn this פרק again. It is not part of the argument; it only marks the end of the section.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the closing formula said at the end of a פרק.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Oaths are two."
phrases.notes: 'שבועות שתים' is the name of this פרק, taken from its first words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק שבועות שתים is finished.
